coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Sophie Maxwell Building
record.summary: Eight-story, 105-unit, 100% affordable workforce housing building at 1212 Maryland St (corner of Humboldt St), the first building completed in the Potrero Power Station redevelopment; designed by Leddy Maytum Stacy Architects, built by Swinerton for Found Middle LP (Associate Capital / Fifth Space), completed August 2025 and opened October 2025 for households at 50-110% AMI.

facts.value: 1212 Maryland St, San Francisco, CA 94107 (corner of Humboldt St)
Found Middle LP (developer of Block 7B; affiliate of Associate Capital, renamed Fifth Space in 2025); project sponsor for design review: California Barrel Company LLC
Leddy Maytum Stacy Architects (design and executive architect; certified SBA-LBE)
Plural (per the firm's own project page; collaborators LMS, CBG Engineers, RMA Irrigation)
Swinerton Builders
The John Stewart Company (JSCO)
105 (98 at the March 2022 design review approval; raised to 105 in the Q1 2023 revised site permit set)
104 restricted units plus 1 manager's unit; 100% affordable
50-110% AMI, averaging 80% AMI (Phase 1 application in 2020 assumed average 55% AMI; 2021 report 55%; 2022-2024 reports 80%)
70 studios, 21 one-bedroom, 14 two-bedroom (as built, per contractor); design review approval: 63 studios, 28 one-bedroom, 7 two-bedroom of 98
approximately 85 (design review memo; 84 per SF YIMBY; D4D maximum for the 7B lot is 85 ft)
83,000 total (design review plan sheet G0.1A); residential area 80,941 GSF (2024 compliance report)
approximately 1,820 (ground floor, cold shell)
residential (100% affordable workforce housing) with ground-floor retail, co-working space and rooftop deck
no vehicle parking; 99 Class I and 9 Class II bicycle spaces
LEED Gold certified; all-electric

First project to use the CalHFA Bond Recycling Program (recycled prior-year tax-exempt bonds) as the primary debt source; financing coordinated with MOHCD, OEWD and JPMorgan Chase; site infrastructure supported by Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District No. 1
JPMorgan Chase (after pitching roughly six banks; negotiations took about seven months)

DA Housing Plan: 100% Affordable Housing Parcels are conveyed by the developer at no cost to the Affordable Housing Developer, in fee or by ground lease, under an Affordable Housing Conveyance Agreement (approved for Block 7B March 19, 2024)
104 100% Affordable Unit Credits toward the Phase 1 30% requirement (about 233 credits), the balance via in-lieu fee credits
about 90% leased as of July-August 2026; about eight applicants per unit at opening
85 for the 7B lot (Block 7 overall: 240-ft highrise tower permitted)
Sophenia 'Sophie' Maxwell, District 10 Supervisor 2001-2011, who led the effort to close the Potrero power plant (closed 2011)
AIA California 2026 Design Award, Citation

images.license_note: Under SB 1214, SF Planning only posts an applicant's full architectural drawings online if the applicant didn't instead submit a reduced massing-diagram-only set for public distribution; when the full drawings are posted, as here in the published Design Review Approval packet, the applicant's permission for public posting is deemed granted and the Department 'shall not be subject to any restrictions on the copying or distribution' of them. Read 2026-09-18.
images.appeal_note: Sunlit ground-level corner rendering with active street life, cyclists and a retail-lined ground floor -- reads cleanly and communicates the design well at any size.

open_questions: Bond amount and issuer for the CalHFA bond-recycling debt (and whether CSCDA or another conduit was involved): looked in the Port memo 10A, the four DA annual reports, the Chronicle (Oct 2023, Aug 2026), SF Standard (Oct 2025), SF YIMBY, Hoodline; no dollar amount for the bonds is stated anywhere.

Total development cost: only Hoodline (Dec 2025, citing the Chronicle) gives '$50 million'; the Standard gives $670,000 per unit (105 x 670,000 = about $70M). The two figures are inconsistent and neither is from a primary document.

Temporary Certificate of Occupancy / First Certificate of Occupancy date: the Port memo says construction was 'completed in August 2025'; no TCO date found. The 2025 DA annual report (due 2026) is not yet on the SF Planning page.

Construction start: the 2023 annual report and press give the groundbreaking ceremony as Oct 12, 2023 (site permit issued Oct 25, 2023), but the 2024 annual report says Found Middle 'commenced construction ... in June 2024' and the 2023 report says the construction contract 'commenced in 2024'. Both are recorded; the June 2024 date is probably the DA-defined commencement.

Design review approval date: the annual reports list Block 7B as 'Approved by Planning Department, 1.5.22; Planning Director Memo dated 3.2.22'. The signed approval letter is dated March 2, 2022; the Jan 5, 2022 event is not otherwise documented.

Parcel: the design review memo lists parent lots 4175/017, 4175/002, 4232/001 and 4232/006; the repo's blklot 4232020 must post-date the Phase 1 Final Map (recorded July 26, 2022). No document in the corpus states the new lot number; 'Lot 10' appears on the LMS plan sheets ('Block 7B - Lot 10').

Land conveyance to Found Middle: the DA Housing Plan requires conveyance at no cost in fee or by ground lease; the approved Affordable Housing Conveyance Agreement (March 19, 2024) is not in the corpus, so fee vs. ground lease and term are unknown.

Lottery: the SF Standard (Oct 15, 2025) says a random lottery would be held later that month, while the May 2025 Housing Plan amendment exempts 100% affordable projects that receive no direct City money from the MOHCD lottery. Whether Sophie Maxwell is a 'City Financed Unit' project is not stated.
Unit mix as built: Swinerton (contractor's own material) gives 70/21/14; the 2022 approval gives 63/28/7 of 98. No City document with the 105-unit mix was found.
Hoodline (Dec 6, 2025) calls it a 'six-story building'; every other source says eight stories. Treated as an error in Hoodline.

No hostable 'now' photograph found: Wikimedia Commons searches for 'Sophie Maxwell Building', 'Potrero Power Station' and 'Dogpatch Power Station' returned no photo of the building (only pre-2011 power plant images). Henrik Kam's photos (SF YIMBY, AIA CA) are not openly licensed; linked only.

Citizen Portal's AI-generated summary of the Oct 2025 opening mentions six Homeless Prenatal Program families among the first residents and 'resident parking'; not used because it is machine-generated from a video and the design approval states no vehicle parking.
